hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about one child - my son Alex. He's 15 years old and lives at home with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask: **Are you responsible for Alex's care?** In other words, do you provide for his daily needs such as food, clothes, and other expenses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm his parent and I take care of all his daily needs - I provide his food, buy his clothes, pay for school things, all of that. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. Just to confirm a few more details:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?** (For example, is he attending secondary school?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in secondary school - Year 10. He's doing his GCSEs next year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me taking care of him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility requirements:

- Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex's care and provide for his daily needs (food, clothes, school expenses)
- Alex lives with you full-time
- He is in full-time education (secondary school, Year 10)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Please note that only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and you'll continue to qualify even when Alex turns 16, as long as he stays in approved education or training (until he's under 20).

**Important reminder:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
